title: Pinned version fallback simulator and deprecation safety playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a deterministic simulator and an operational playbook for exercising fallback paths when customers pin model versions. The simulator should model region- and variant-level fallbacks, estimate request-level latency/cost/regression risk, and produce a risk heatmap that feeds into Console runbooks and automated canary gates. The playbook will define staged deprecation flows, rollback triggers, and mitigations for compatibility regressions.
background: Customers often pin model versions for stability. During deprecations, capacity shortages, or regional outages the platform must choose safe fallback variants and regions without causing quality regressions or SLA violations. Existing work focuses on runtime fallback routing and compatibility checks, but we lack a predictive simulation that quantifies user-visible risk prior to eviction and a single playbook that ties simulation outputs to rollout decisions.
design_decisions: Create an offline simulator that replays traffic traces (sampled token-sequences + metadata) and applies configurable fallback policies to compute per-route impact metrics
Represent variant compatibility as a numeric score (0-100) derived from model eval sets + schema checks; use thresholds to gate automated fallbacks
Simulate cold-warm KV cache effects and batching changes to estimate latency distribution shifts
Expose simulator output via Console: scenario diff, top-k affected customers, and suggested mitigations
Integrate with rollout engine to allow 'simulate -> approve -> staged rollout' workflow
Keep simulation deterministic and idempotent for reproducible incident postmortems
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest a 24h traffic sample and run a full fallback scenario in under 30 minutes for a single region cluster
Simulator produces per-route metrics: token-cost delta, p95 latency delta, compatibility regression probability, and estimated error-rate increase
Console shows scenario heatmap and exports suggested staged rollout steps (canary cohorts, throttle percentages)
Automated canary gate can be driven by simulator outputs and will stop rollout if regression probability > configured threshold
Playbook documents a step-by-step deprecation flow, rollback conditions, and communication templates for affected customers
End-to-end test with a non-prod tenant demonstrating a simulated deprecation and an automated stop/rollback

risks_mitigation: Risk: Simulator underestimates cold-cache latency. Mitigation: include conservative cold-start multipliers and run live verification experiments.
Risk: Compatibility score misses semantic regression. Mitigation: require human review for scores near threshold and tie to eval-suite failures.
Risk: Simulator runtime expensive for large traces. Mitigation: stratified sampling and fast-path heuristics for low-impact routes.
Risk: Automated rollback triggers cause churn. Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum observation windows before triggering rollbacks.
notes: Prototype accepted for FY25 Q4 experiment; this ticket scopes productionization and Console integration.
We should reuse existing eval harness and evaluator schemas to compute compatibility scores rather than inventing a new format.
Coordinate with legal/security early because deprecation notifications require documented audit trail and opt-out hooks.
